title: Optimise NPS for Higher Returns & a Bigger Retirement Corpus
description: The National Pension System (NPS) offers a low-cost, market-linked avenue for retirement planning. Optimising your asset allocation, especially increasing equ.

faq.q: Can I change my Pension Fund Manager (PFM) in NPS?
faq.a: Yes, you can change your PFM once in a financial year. You can do this by logging into your NPS account online and submitting a request.

faq.q: What happens if I don't choose an asset allocation?
faq.a: If you don't make an active choice, your funds will automatically be invested under the Auto Choice (Lifecycle Fund) LC50, which starts with 50% equity exposure and gradually reduces it with age.

faq.q: Are Tier II NPS contributions tax-deductible?
faq.a: Generally, Tier II contributions are not tax-deductible for private sector employees. However, government employees can claim a deduction under Section 80C for Tier II contributions with a three-year lock-in period.

faq.q: What are the withdrawal rules for NPS at maturity?
faq.a: At age 60, you can withdraw up to 60% of your corpus as a lump sum, which is entirely tax-exempt. The remaining 40% must be used to purchase an annuity from an IRDAI-regulated life insurance company, which provides a regular pension.

faq.q: How often should I rebalance my NPS portfolio?
faq.a: You are allowed to change your asset allocation once in a financial year. It's advisable to review your portfolio annually and rebalance if your actual allocation deviates significantly from your target, or if your risk profile changes.
Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can open an NPS account. The contributions are subject to FEMA regulations and income tax provisions applicable to NRIs.
